title: Account number under an account label is not a medical record number
rationale: A labeled account number names a billing or financial role, not the medical record role. For the medical record number kind the token is not an instance. Whether the account number is itself sensitive depends on account type and holder, which the sources leave open. Synthetic value: the SYNTH- prefix marks it as fabricated, generated by the authored rule 'SYNTH- plus a letter and six digits', not derived from any record, next to no name, date or clinical detail, and not tested against any service.

reasons: HL7 AN and FHIR Account.identifier define an account number as its own role; the label vocabulary is project-authored.
Sensitivity of an account number alone is context-dependent; domains are candidates.
ambiguity.wouldSettle: An authority statement on whether a bare account number is person-linked, by account type and holder.

provenance.inference: Project inference: the invalid outcome is relative to the MRN kind only; it does not say the token is non-sensitive.

title: Encounter identifier under an encounter label is not a medical record number
rationale: An encounter or visit identifier names one episode of care, not the patient's record. For the medical record number kind the token is not an instance; whether a bare encounter id is a person-linked identifier is not established because the cited definition links the person through a separate element. Synthetic value: the SYNTH- prefix marks it as fabricated, generated by the authored rule 'SYNTH- plus a letter and six digits', not derived from any record, next to no name, date or clinical detail, and not tested against any service.

reasons: FHIR Encounter.identifier and HL7 VN are separate roles; person linkage is a separate element.
Domains are candidates pending a source on bare encounter ids.
ambiguity.wouldSettle: An authority or provider statement on whether an encounter or visit id alone is person-linked.

provenance.inference: Project inference: the invalid outcome is relative to the MRN kind only.

title: Patient identifier label whose relation to the medical record number is not established
rationale: HL7 defines the patient internal identifier (unique within an assigning authority) separately from the medical record number (unique within a set of medical records). A bare patient ID label does not establish which role the value has, so identity as an MRN is not established. Synthetic value: the SYNTH- prefix marks it as fabricated, generated by the authored rule 'SYNTH- plus a letter and six digits', not derived from any record, next to no name, date or clinical detail, and not tested against any service.

reasons: PI, PT and MR are distinct codes; a patient ID label does not select one.
Whether a separate patient-identifier kind is warranted is open (see docs/research/clinical-record-identifiers.md).
ambiguity.wouldSettle: A provider-documented source listing field labels with their identifier roles, or a decision to model a patient-identifier kind.

provenance.inference: Project inference: the sensitivity is sensitive because a patient-level identifier is a patient identifier in either role; the MRN identity is the unestablished part.
